title: One cycle of the polymerase chain reaction
caption: Each cycle heats to separate the strands (about 95 °C), cools so primers can bind to each end of the target (50–65 °C), and warms to 72 °C so heat-stable Taq polymerase can extend them. Each cycle roughly doubles the target, so copies = initial number × 2ⁿ.
alt: Three boxes in order: denaturation at about 95 degrees, annealing at 50 to 65 degrees, and extension at about 72 degrees, then the cycle repeats.
description: Denaturation, about 95 °C: heat separates the two strands.
Annealing, about 50–65 °C: primers bind to each end of the target.
Extension, about 72 °C: Taq polymerase adds nucleotides from the primers.
The cycle repeats 25–35 times, doubling the target each time.
